docRequirement: glossary.md:231 (§ Project trust) binds project-trust acceptance to per-project-directory persistence with ONE exception: "Acceptance is saved per project directory, except your home directory, where trust is held for the current session only and the prompt reappears on each launch." The same line says what the grant buys — trust "gates auto-installation of marketplace plugins and execution of project-defined hooks" and makes the directory's `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json` and other config files take effect — so the home-directory carve-out is a security narrowing, not cosmetics.
current: The fork treats $HOME as an ordinary project root and persists its grant like any other. (1) `ProjectHandleService.validateProjectDirectory` is the sole raw-path ingress (packages/shared/src/projects/project-handle-service.ts:140-156) and it accepts $HOME: `validateCandidateProjectPath` (:250-274) rejects only non-absolute paths and managed paths, and `isManagedPath` (:276-278) matches only `CONFIG_DIR` plus injected managed workspace roots (:124-133). (2) `resolveProjectIdentity` returns `persistence: 'stable'` for any path the platform can stat — `process-only` is reached ONLY when `statIdentity` throws or reports `ino === 0n` (packages/shared/src/projects/project-identity.ts:116-133); there is no home-directory branch, and `grep -rain "homedir|process.env.HOME" packages/shared/src/projects packages/shared/src/capabilities` returns nothing (exit 1). (3) `ProjectTrustStore.record` therefore writes the home grant to `CONFIG_DIR/project-trust.json` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-trust-store.ts:135-158) and `resolve` reads it back for any `'stable'` identity (:114-128), so the grant survives a restart. (4) Nothing upstream carves home out either: the RPC `projects.SET_TRUST` handler passes the ref straight through (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/projects.ts:78-86), `SessionManager.setProjectTrust` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:14537-14613) has no path special-case, and the renderer opens `ProjectTrustDialog` purely on `trustState === 'unknown'` at pick time (apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/ChatPage.tsx:339-341, apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/settings/WorkspaceSettingsPage.tsx:251). (5) The grant is material: project-scope instruction/skill/agent/MCP/hook/permission records are emitted only when `context.projectTrustState === 'trusted'` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:995-1024), project `.nessy-agent/config.toml` defaults load only when trusted (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:8878-8880), the trusted-project plugin policy overlay requires it (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:951), and `isPiLspProvisioningAllowed` requires it (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2090-2091).
divergence: The session-only trust mechanism EXISTS and works — `persistence: 'process-only'` keeps a decision in `ProjectTrustStore.processOnly` (project-trust-store.ts:101, :115-121, :149-152) and it expires with the process because the fingerprint is salted with a per-process random value (project-identity.ts:56, :118). The delta is that the home directory never reaches it: `persistence` is decided solely by stat success, so `$HOME` is classified `'stable'` and its grant is persisted. This is a missing one-branch carve-out in `resolveProjectIdentity`, not a missing mechanism and not a wrong field name. Second, smaller delta: even once the grant lapses, no surface re-prompts — `ProjectTrustDialog` is opened only from a directory-pick callback, never from a restored session whose project resolves `unknown`, so the doc's "the prompt reappears on each launch" leg needs its own edit.

change.what: Add `homeDir?: string` to `ResolveProjectIdentityOptions` (:46-50) as a test seam defaulting to `os.homedir()`. In `resolveProjectIdentity`, after `canonicalPath` is computed (:107-114), canonicalize the home directory through the SAME injected `realpath` (try/catch falling back to `resolve(homeDir)`) and widen the existing fallback condition at :117 from `if (!identity)` to `if (!identity || canonicalPath === canonicalHome)`, reusing the unchanged process-only body (:118-125). ~10 lines including the import. Only the home directory itself — a subdirectory of home must stay `'stable'`. Extend the module header (:16-21) to name the home carve-out as the second route to `process-only` and cite `glossary.md:231` with the verbatim sentence, so the reason lives next to the branch.

REQUIRED compatibility guard, not optional. `if (defaultProject.projectKey && selectedProject?.projectKey !== defaultProject.projectKey) selectedProject = undefined` followed by `throw new Error('workspace-default-project-invalid')` (:8867-8872). A process-only key can never match a stored one, so a `workspace.json` that already holds `defaults.defaultProject.projectKey` for $HOME (written by today's code — `setWorkspaceDefaultProject` persists the key only for `'stable'`, :14512-14515) would make EVERY new session in that workspace throw after the identity change. Add `&& selectedProject?.persistence === 'stable'` to the comparison so a process-only resolution falls back to the workingDirectory match. This also fixes the same latent break for genuine unstable-filesystem projects (network mount reporting inode 0).

Same compatibility guard: `const staleHint = !!record.projectKey && record.projectKey !== resolved.projectKey` fires for a pre-existing $HOME recent record once its identity turns process-only, which writes a quarantine record and emits `recent-project-stale` (:167-172, :245-252) — and throws `recent-project-stale` on the `rejectIdentityChange` path (:168-171). Add `&& resolved.persistence === 'stable'`. The rest of the store already handles process-only correctly (`recordValidatedProject` omits `projectKey`, :108, :117; the updated record deletes it, :176-181).

Positive path: an injected `homeDir` whose stat SUCCEEDS resolves `persistence: 'process-only'` and a key that differs between two `processSalt` values. Negative/boundary: a subdirectory of that home resolves `'stable'`; home reached through a symlink still resolves `'process-only'` (the comparison is on the realpath, matching the existing symlink-swap block at :75).

One test: `record(homeIdentity, 'trusted')` returns `persistence: 'process-only'`, writes nothing to the trust file, and a FRESH `ProjectTrustStore` instance (restart simulation) resolves `{ state: 'none' }` — the exact probe the challenger ran, pinned. Keep the existing stable-identity persistence test as the positive control.

End-to-end through the ingress: `validateProjectDirectory(ws, home)` still issues a handle (home is NOT refused — the doc allows trusting it, only session-scoped); `setProjectTrust(..., 'trusted')` reports `trusted` inside the process; a second service built with a fresh `ProjectTrustStore` over the same file reports `trustState: 'unknown'`. Inject `identityOptions.homeDir` — the service already forwards `identityOptions` (project-handle-service.ts:121, :142, :191).

Second leg of the doc sentence ("the prompt reappears on each launch"), separable from the persistence fix. Today the dialog opens only from the directory-pick callback (:339-341), so once a home grant lapses the user gets no prompt and project layers simply go quiet. Open `ProjectTrustDialog` when a restored session's project resolves `trustState: 'unknown'`; the value is already on the wire as `security.projectTrustState` (packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:253), so no new wire field is needed. Mirror it in apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/settings/WorkspaceSettingsPage.tsx:251 for the workspace default project.

blastRadius: Crosses a persistence boundary in three files and a package boundary — a risk trigger in this repo. (1) `CONFIG_DIR/project-trust.json`: any already-persisted $HOME row becomes unreachable after the change (a process-only identity never reads the file, project-trust-store.ts:115-121) — harmless but a one-time prune is nice-to-have. (2) `workspace.json` → `defaults.defaultProject.projectKey`: without the SessionManager.ts:8867 guard this throws `workspace-default-project-invalid` on every new session in a workspace whose default project is $HOME. (3) `recent-projects.json`: without the recent-store.ts:167 guard the $HOME entry is quarantined on first re-issue. (4) `projectKey` is also the project-scope capability-policy key — `CapabilityPolicyStore` persists `{kind:'project', projectKey}` overrides (packages/shared/src/capabilities/policy-store.ts:61, :207-215, :285-293, :373-376) and `selectedCapabilityScope` (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:971-976) derives from it, so a per-launch-rotating home key orphans any project-scope override recorded for $HOME; acceptable (an untrusted project contributes nothing anyway) but it must be a decided consequence, not a surprise. (5) Readers of the gate: native-sources.ts:995, resolver.ts:2241 + :1623-1634 (hook trust), SessionManager.ts:2090-2100 (Pi LSP provisioning), :3150-3181 (`security.projectTrustState` in the Pi harness runtime snapshot, validated by packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:182-192 — read-only, shape unchanged), :4274/:4579/:4764/:4845/:5021, storage-runtime.ts:951, base-agent.ts:900 + :1209. (6) Tests to update/verify: packages/shared/src/projects/__tests__/{project-identity,project-handle-service,recent-store,workspace-project-contract-corpus}.test.ts, packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/project-trust-store.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/__tests__/projects.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/project-mutation.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/domain/capabilities/__tests__/context.test.ts. (7) No imported-plugin path and no protocol DTO change: `IssuedProjectHandle.trustState` and `SetProjectTrustInput` (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:233-234) keep their shape.
userImpact: Concrete and security-relevant. Pick your home folder as a session's project folder or as a workspace default project (Chat working-directory picker, or Settings → Workspace → Default project folder), click Trust once in the dialog, and the grant is written to disk forever: every later launch silently loads and executes everything project-scope under the whole home tree — `~/.nessy-agent/hooks.json` hook commands, `~/.nessy-agent/mcp.json` servers, project skills/agents/permissions (native-sources.ts:995-1024), project `.nessy-agent/config.toml` defaults, and Pi LSP provisioning — with no re-prompt. In Claude Code that same click lasts one session and the dialog comes back next launch. Because the home tree is where every unrelated repo, download and cache lives, this is the one directory where a persisted grant has effectively unbounded reach. The user sees nothing to tell them apart: the dialog and the trusted badge look identical to a normal project's.
notes: Subsystem note against the sibling-symbol trap: this is PROJECT trust (packages/shared/src/projects/ + packages/shared/src/capabilities/project-trust-store.ts), not the permission-mode machinery in packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts, and not the per-capability `CapabilityTrustStore` reached via `inputs.resolveTrust` at resolver.ts:1625 and :1721 — those are a different store with a different key (executable hash), and confusing them is the easy wrong answer here.
